native_metadata_original.title: A Martin kernel with isolated Harnack contact in an annulus
native_metadata_original.description:
For the annulus 1 < |z| < e, with base point a = exp(1/2), the normalized minimal Martin kernel at the inner-boundary point -1 is strictly below the envelope of normalized positive harmonic functions throughout a punctured neighborhood of a. Four explicit positive harmonic competitors yield a uniform first-order gap in every direction. Direct Green-kernel construction and harmonic reflection establish the Martin limit and minimality.

This gives a negative answer to the equality-along-a-Green-line extension in Hayman and Lingham, Research Problems in Function Theory, arXiv:1809.07200v2, Problem 7.42, attributed to Arsove and Johnson. The statement concerns equality along a line issuing from the base point; it does not exclude isolated contact farther away. A dated, bounded priority audit accompanies the authored verification package. An addendum proves that a simpler punctured-disc counterexample is an elementary deduction from classical positive-harmonic representations, including Kohn (1966); this does not establish prior recognition of the Green-line consequence or yield the smooth-annulus theorem. No claim of first historical resolution or certification of current worldwide openness is made.

The deposit contains a concise research note and authored proof source, independent adversarial reviews and reproducibility materials. OpenAI tools were used extensively in solving, drafting and verifying the result. This is an unrefereed preprint, with no completed human peer review or formal proof-assistant certification claimed. Integrity checks and numerical checks do not replace the analytic proof.
references: W. K. Hayman and E. F. Lingham, Research Problems in Function Theory (New Edition), arXiv:1809.07200v2 (2018), Problem 7.42 and Update 7.42, pp. 173-174.
D. A. Herron, The Harnack and other conformally invariant metrics, Kodai Math. J. 10 (1987), 9-19. https://doi.org/10.2996/kmj/1138037356
H. S. Bear and W. Smith, A tale of two conformally invariant metrics, J. Math. Anal. Appl. 318 (2006), 498-506. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmaa.2005.05.065
H. Shiga, Conformal invariants defined by harmonic functions on Riemann surfaces, J. Math. Soc. Japan 68 (2016), 441-458. https://doi.org/10.2969/jmsj/06810441
J. Kohn, Die Harnacksche Metrik in der Theorie der harmonischen Funktionen, Math. Z. 91 (1966), 50-64, especially p. 63. https://doi.org/10.1007/BF01113851

complete_manuscript_abstract_TeX: For the annulus $1<|z|<e$, we exhibit a normalized minimal Martin kernel that is strictly below the envelope of normalized positive harmonic functions at every point of a punctured neighborhood of the base point. Four explicit positive harmonic competitors give a uniform first-order gap in every direction. The result disproves the extension to multiply connected domains of the equality-along-a-Green-line property in Hayman and Lingham's Problem 7.42, attributed to Arsove and Johnson. We give direct constructions of the Green and Martin kernels and a proof of minimality. The broader negative conclusion also has a simpler punctured-disc derivation from classical results; our theorem gives a smooth-annulus construction. OpenAI tools were used extensively in developing and independently checking the argument. This note has not undergone human peer review or formal proof-assistant verification.

source_preprint_README:
# Annular Martin-kernel research note

This folder is the preprint package for PR810, problem2307042 / AMR-022-7042,
Hayman–Lingham Problem7.42. The exact theorem and all assumptions are stated in
the concise research note. Repository acceptance and publication receipts are
maintained separately from this frozen prepublication verification package.

## Build and inspect

Build with a current TeX installation (the preparation used Tectonic):

    mkdir -p output/pdf
    tectonic --outdir output/pdf note.tex

The source uses standard article, geometry, amsmath, amssymb, amsthm, fontenc,
lmodern and hyperref packages. A successful build proves only that the document
compiles. Mathematical acceptance rests on the analytic proof and independent
reviews, not document compilation, checksums or numerical sampling.

After extracting verification.zip, work in its preprint/ directory. The
standard-library diagnostic script at ../math_review_01/reproduce_checks.py
recomputes its output file; this is diagnostic verification, not a proof. Its
explicit invariant guards remain active with normal and optimized Python. The
correction receipt records the historical script and negative-control tests.
Rebuild the PDF as above before running python3 build_package.py. PDF creation
timestamps may differ; byte-for-byte reproduction of compiled PDFs is not
claimed. The supporting archive is assembled by build_package.py from an explicit list
of authored materials. Its MANIFEST.json gives file hashes and sizes and does
not hash itself. No third-party PDFs, raw source extracts, private credentials
or private project coordination records belong in the public package. Bounded
public QUEUE-delta and research-log records are included as provenance.

## Disclosure and scope

OpenAI tools were used extensively in solving, drafting and independent
adversarial verification. This is an unrefereed preprint; no completed human
peer review or proof-assistant certification is claimed. The theorem excludes
contact in a punctured neighborhood of the base and equality throughout a
Green line issuing from it. It does not exclude isolated contact farther away.
Priority statements are limited to the accompanying dated audit.

Author: Alec Kriebel, independent researcher.
ORCID: https://orcid.org/0009-0001-9320-500X.
Paper and authored supplementary materials: CC BY4.0.

The October12 priority audit in the supporting archive expands the historical
source-status packet with Shiga, Köhn and Leutwiler and a full final-title
Bear–Smith author manuscript. Original frozen packets retain their historical
inspection limits; the new dated audit is the current source/priority record.
No first-resolution or current-worldwide-openness certification is claimed.

The later punctured-disc priority addendum records a simple negative example
deduced from older classical formulas, including the minimal-kernel
classification on page63 of Kohn (1966). It distinguishes this deduction from
a located historical resolution and from the smooth-annulus theorem. This
addendum qualifies the broader historical context of the earlier audit.

copy_contract.theorem: D={z in C:1<|z|<e}, a=exp(1/2), inner-boundary point xi=-1. Its normalized minimal Martin kernel K_xi(a)=1 lies strictly below H_a(z) at every z in a sufficiently small punctured neighborhood U\{a}.
copy_contract.envelope: H_a(z)=sup{h(z):h>0 harmonic on D, h(a)<=1}; H_a(a)=1.
copy_contract.scope: Excludes equality along any nontrivial curve/Green line issuing from a; does not exclude isolated contact farther away.
copy_contract.mechanism: Log-cylinder periodization constructs Green/Martin kernels; boundary reflection and maximum principle prove minimality. Four globally positive normalized harmonic competitors and a uniform all-direction first-order gap yield local strict inequality by a common Taylor bound; no smoothness of H_a is assumed.
copy_contract.attribution: Hayman-Lingham2018 Problem7.42/Updatepp173-174, attributedArsove-Johnson; classical strip kernels/reflection/maximum principle. Herron, Bear-Smith, Shiga related metricwork. Köhn1966p63 and Bear-Smithauthor-manuscriptProp2.6 give classical punctured-disc context.
copy_contract.priority: Smooth annulus with two nondegenerate boundary components. Broader negative conclusion also follows by an elementary punctured-disc deduction from classical positive-harmonic representations; this does not establish prior recognition of the Green-line consequence or yield smooth-annulus theorem. No first historical resolution/current worldwide openness claim.
